head: bf42c12
specSourceGaps: lib/phlimbo-ea/CLAUDE.md is stale (inventory stops at V2, never mentions V3) — not usable as a V3 intent source.

SolvencyDetermination.md does not mention MigratorV2V3 at ALL (grep for 'Migrator' returns nothing). The migrator's only intent sources are the story commit messages and its own NatSpec. Findings F-08-01/02/03 are therefore anchored on commit text + NatSpec only; no design-doc criteria were invented.

storyVerdicts.verdict: FAITHFUL — complete, no deviation, story intent is safe (no Law-1 override)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Freeze accPromoPerShare during Flushing at the accrual site
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: src/PhlimboV3.sol:757 — `if (address(promoToken) != address(0) && promoPhase != PromoPhase.Flushing)` inside _updatePool. Gate is at the accrual site, not on callers.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: collectReward (permissionless), setDesiredAPY, setDepletionDuration all reach _updatePool while paused — all three must be covered
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: All three reach _updatePool (L555 collectReward, L232 setDesiredAPY commit branch, L249 setDepletionDuration) and all three are now gated by the single accrual-site check. Verified by enumerating every _updatePool caller (L232,249,343,368,389,413,555,581,628,675): stake/withdraw/claim/startPromotion are whenNotPaused (unreachable while flushing); topUpPromotion/setPromoDepletionDuration require phase==Active (unreachable while Flushing); beginFlush (L413) calls _updatePool while phase is still Active so its final accrual is preserved. No ungated accrual path remains during Flushing.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Mirror the gate in pendingPromo so the view cannot over-report mid-rotation
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: src/PhlimboV3.sol:884 — same `promoPhase != PromoPhase.Flushing` conjunct in the view. View and accrual agree.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Correct the three stale invariant comments that attributed the accumulator freeze to pausing
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Exactly three comment blocks corrected: header §2(b) (L32-38), accPromoPerShare state-var docstring (L121-127), beginFlush @dev (L400-409). Each now attributes the freeze to the _updatePool phase gate and explicitly says NOT to the pause. Count matches the story exactly.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Includes forge fmt normalization of the touched file (declared scope)
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: `forge fmt --check src/PhlimboV3.sol` exits 0 at HEAD. The formatting churn (constructor, getPromoInfo, getPoolInfo, getPendingAPYInfo, require reflows) is attributable to forge fmt. Full-diff read confirms the ONLY semantic deltas in d61a7a3 are the two `promoPhase != PromoPhase.Flushing` conjuncts (L757, L884). Nothing else changed behaviour.

lifecycleCompositionChecks: startPromotion (L335-355) calls _updatePool() BEFORE assigning promoToken, and finalizePromotion zeroes promoToken — so a stale lastRewardTime spanning a flush window can never retro-accrue against the NEXT promo token. The gate composes correctly with the rotation lifecycle; this was the most likely way to reintroduce H-01 and it is closed.

abortFlush is solvency-neutral as SolvencyDetermination.md §4 claims — retro-accrual on the abort path is capped by promoRewardBalance and balance-conserving. It does, however, introduce a path-dependence the story did not consider — see F-08-03.
storyVerdicts.law1Assessment: SAFE. The story's intended behaviour (freeze accrual during Flushing) is the correct fix for V3-H-01 and introduces no new exploit. The freeze is enforced at the single accrual site, making it future-proof against new call sites, as the story argues.

storyVerdicts.verdict: SUBSTANTIALLY FAITHFUL with 3 deviations (all Low) — no scope creep; every src change was declared in the commit message. Story intent is NOT unsafe (no Law-1 override), but trade-off (a) is a genuine Law-3 owner footgun.

acceptanceCriteria.status: MET (byte-identical) — but see F-08-01: the copied helper carries an OPEN known defect (V3-L-02)

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: _forward banks failed forwards into per-user unclaimable mapping + emits RewardForwardFailed instead of reverting, so the cursor always advances
acceptanceCriteria.status: MET for the PoC'd blocklist vector; NOT unconditional — see F-08-01
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: src/MigratorV2V3.sol:285-290. A blocklisted USDT-style recipient reverts inside the call → callSuccess==false → banks. V3-M-01's PoC'd vector is genuinely closed.

src/MigratorV2V3.sol:227-233. Entry zeroed BEFORE safeTransfer; nonReentrant. Reverting safeTransfer on the user-initiated path is correct and deliberate. Arbitrary `token` param is not exploitable — unclaimable[token][msg.sender] can only be non-zero for phUSD/rewardToken/promoToken, and amount==0 reverts.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: withdrawAll extended to sweep live promo token; WithdrawnAll extended with promo amount
acceptanceCriteria.status: MET (declared scope, not creep) — but see F-08-02 and F-08-04
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: src/MigratorV2V3.sol:243-265; event widened to (address,uint256,uint256,uint256) in IMigratorV2V3.sol:57-59.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Recovery-note NatSpec rewritten (audit F-01): drop the unreachable 'exclude from seed list' escape, document the banked-claims trade-off
acceptanceCriteria.status: MET at the header (L57-68) — but the function-level @dev was left stale, see F-08-02
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: The false 'operational escape is to exclude such addresses from the seed list' text is gone from the header.

storyVerdicts.scopeCreepAssessment: CLEAN. Every src/interface change in ef98cd9 maps to a bullet in its own commit message (helper copy, _forward banking, claimUnclaimable, withdrawAll promo leg, WithdrawnAll widening, NatSpec rewrite). The `unclaimable` public mapping + its interface view are the necessary mechanics of a declared bullet. Test/snapshot commits (27482c2, bf42c12) touch ZERO src files (verified via git log --stat).
storyVerdicts.law1Assessment: Story intent is NOT unsafe. Trade-off (b) is sound (see tradeOffAssessment). Trade-off (a) is a deliberate, documented owner design choice — Law 3 trusts it — but its OBSERVABILITY gap makes it a footgun (F-08-02). Neither warrants a story-unsafe escalation: no unprivileged attacker path, no theft, harm is owner-action-gated and owner-reversible.

tradeOffAssessment.tradeOff: (a) claimUnclaimable reverts unbacked after a full withdrawAll sweep — commit calls this a 'documented trade-off'
tradeOffAssessment.verdict: The DESIGN CHOICE is safe and Law-3 trusted; the OBSERVABILITY GAP around it is a genuine footgun → F-08-02 (Low).
reasoning: Not a Law-1 escalation: requires an owner action, no unprivileged attacker path, no theft, harm bounded by banked amounts and reversible by out-of-band reimbursement.

House precedent makes the choice defensible: PhlimboV3.finalizePromotion ALSO sweeps unclaimablePromo to leftoverRecipient and zeroes it — the house baseline FORFEITS banked failed-transfer claims outright, with no per-user claim at all. MigratorV2V3 is strictly MORE generous (it grants a surviving per-user claim). Law 3: do not report a deliberate, documented design the owner chose.
BUT the surprise is not the rule — it is the rule's INVISIBILITY. See F-08-02: the owner cannot see the liability they are about to confiscate.

tradeOffAssessment.tradeOff: (b) _forward banking converts a hard brick into silent per-user debt whose only signal is a RewardForwardFailed event
tradeOffAssessment.verdict: SAFE — not a finding. The 'silent' framing overstates it.
reasoning: The debt is NOT signal-only: `unclaimable(address,address)` is a public view declared in the interface (IMigratorV2V3.sol:122), so an affected user can read their own balance on-chain without event scraping.
The debt is backed 1:1 by construction — the failed transfer means the tokens never left the contract.

Balance-diff bracketing is not corrupted by banked funds: phUSDBefore/stableBefore/promoBefore include previously banked amounts, but every credit is a DELTA (after - before), so banked funds are never re-counted or double-forwarded on a straggler second pass.
Banked entries are keyed by token ADDRESS, so a promo rotation does not orphan a claim.
Reentrancy-safe: migrate and claimUnclaimable share the nonReentrant guard; CEI on the claim path.
Strictly better than the alternative it replaced: reverting bricked EVERYONE (that was V3-M-01); banking localizes harm to the affected user, who retains a claim.
CAVEAT: (b)'s safety is conditional on (a) not being exercised — the banked debt's only backing is the contract balance that withdrawAll can zero. That composition is exactly what F-08-02 tracks.

ledgerReconciliation.label: V3-F-01
ledgerReconciliation.title: FAITHFULNESS: MigratorV2V3 documented in-contract recovery path is unreachable while bricked (story-023)
ledgerReconciliation.verdict: GENUINELY RESOLVED — propose `fixed` (human applies). This is NOT a comment-only paper-over.
reasoning: The instruction's trap — 'rewriting a comment is not the same as fixing a code deviation' — was tested explicitly and does NOT apply here. BOTH sides of the deviation moved, not just the doc.
DOC side: the false promise ('As with MigratorV1V2, the operational escape is to exclude such addresses from the seed list') is deleted from the header (ef98cd9).

CODE side: F-01's deviation was 'doc promises in-contract recovery the code lacks'. story-025 gave the code REAL in-contract recovery on two axes: (1) _forward banking means a bad recipient no longer pins the cursor, so the straggler-exclusion escape is no longer NEEDED; (2) claimUnclaimable is an actual in-contract recovery path that did not exist before. The doc is now weaker than the code, not stronger.

The L126 reseed guard (`require(!seeded || migrateIterator == -1, 'Pass in progress')`) is UNCHANGED — but it is no longer load-bearing for F-01, because the pass no longer gets pinned by the recipient class F-01 was about.

NARROW RESIDUAL, disclosed for honesty (Law 1, recall over tidiness): the abi.decode path in F-08-01 can still pin the cursor mid-pass, and in that state the reseed guard still blocks reseeding AND the rewritten doc no longer mentions any escape at all. That residual is carried by F-08-01 (new entry), NOT by F-01 — F-01's specific cited deviation is closed.

ledgerReconciliation.label: V3-F-02
ledgerReconciliation.title: FAITHFULNESS: PhlimboV3 'the flush must never brick' invariant undermined by unchecked abi.decode (story-022)
ledgerReconciliation.verdict: STILL ACCURATE AND UNCHANGED — premise did NOT shift. Keep `open`. Line numbers shift only.
reasoning: Re-read the current code rather than assuming. story-024's three comment rewrites were ALL about the accPromoPerShare freeze (header §2(b), accPromoPerShare state-var docstring, beginFlush @dev). NONE of them touched F-02's premise.
F-02's cited invariant text is verbatim intact at src/PhlimboV3.sol:427: 'banked into `unclaimablePromo` — the flush must never brick.'

F-02's cited code is behaviourally identical at src/PhlimboV3.sol:818-820: `return callSuccess && (returndata.length == 0 || abi.decode(returndata, (bool)));` — the unchecked abi.decode with no length check survives. The only delta in the range is forge fmt joining the two-line statement into one.
The deviation therefore holds exactly as originally described. F-02 remains open; its security twin V3-L-02 (also open) still owns the DoS severity — not double-counted.

ledgerReconciliation.label: V3-M-01
ledgerReconciliation.title: MigratorV2V3 reverting/blocklisted reward recipient bricks the V2->V3 migration chunk
ledgerReconciliation.verdict: SUBSTANTIVELY FIXED for the PoC'd vector — but DO NOT auto-flip to `fixed`; a narrow brick path survives (F-08-01).
ledgerReconciliation.proposedStatus: propose fixed ONLY after PoC replay; residual tracked separately as F-08-01
reasoning: Root cause named in the fingerprint — 'reverting-reward-forward-in-unskippable-loop ... no-in-contract-recovery' — is addressed on both halves: forwarding is now non-reverting (_forward/_tryTransfer) and in-contract recovery now exists (claimUnclaimable).
The PoC'd vector (blocklisted recipient, workspace/phlimbo-ea/test/poc-m01-migrator-brick.t.sol) is closed: a blocklist revert yields callSuccess==false → banks → cursor advances.

INCOMPLETE-FIX CAUTION (CLAUDE.md: an incomplete fix reads as done): the loop can STILL revert for the token class in F-08-01/V3-L-02 (transfer returning 1-31 bytes, or a 32-byte non-bool). That class is narrow and token-gated, and I do not rate it as an incomplete fix of M-01's root cause — but the 'pass can brick' OUTCOME is not 100% eliminated, so the residual must stay visible rather than vanish inside an M-01 closure.
Recommend: /recheck phlimbo-ea V3-M-01 to replay the PoC against bf42c12 before a human flips the status.

mechanicalCommitVerification.verdict: CLEAN — both .gas-snapshot regen commits are mechanical only, no smuggled logic
evidence: Filtered every +/- line in `git diff 7045a96..bf42c12 -- .gas-snapshot` against the strict pattern `^[+-][A-Za-z0-9_]+:test[A-Za-z0-9_]*\(\) \(gas: [0-9]+\)$` — ZERO non-conforming lines. Every changed line is a test-name/gas-number pair. No config, no settings, no prose smuggled in.

findings.specText: story-025 (ef98cd9) NatSpec, src/MigratorV2V3.sol:57-61: "Recovery note: reward forwarding never reverts. Each delta is sent with the non-reverting `_tryTransfer`; if a recipient cannot receive a token (e.g. a blocklisted address), the amount is banked into the per-user `unclaimable` mapping and `RewardForwardFailed` is emitted, so the cursor always advances and a single bad recipient can never brick a pass." Also src/MigratorV2V3.sol:270-272: "Non-reverting ERC20 transfer used by the migration pass: a single blocklisted or otherwise reverting recipient must not brick migrate."
findings.specSource: git commit ef98cd9 body ("Copy house _tryTransfer helper from PhlimboV3; add _forward that banks failed forwards ... instead of reverting, so the cursor always advances") + src/MigratorV2V3.sol header NatSpec
findings.actualBehavior: `_tryTransfer` (L275-278) is a byte-identical copy of PhlimboV3's helper, including its unchecked `abi.decode(returndata, (bool))` with no length check. For a token whose `transfer` returns non-empty return-data shorter than 32 bytes (or a 32-byte word that is not a valid bool), `abi.decode` REVERTS inside `_tryTransfer`. The revert propagates through `_forward` → the `migrate` loop → the whole chunk, pinning `migrateIterator`. Forwarding therefore does NOT 'never revert', and such a recipient/token CAN still brick a pass.
findings.deviation: The story's claim is UNCONDITIONAL ('never reverts', 'can never brick a pass'); the helper it copied only delivers non-reversion for tokens that revert-or-return-clean. story-025 knowingly copied the 'house' helper while its defect was live and OPEN in the ledger as V3-L-02, and then upgraded the prose to a stronger guarantee than the helper can honour. The exposure is materially worse in the migrator than in PhlimboV3: `promoToken` is an arbitrary owner-selected partner token, and it is the one leg of `_forward` (L203) carrying a non-house token.
findings.impactNote: Narrow and token-gated (rules out the primary blocklist vector — USDT-style blocklist reverts return no data and bank correctly). No fund loss; owner-recoverable. Rated Low, consistent with the prior run's rating of the identical class as V3-L-02 (Low).
findings.recommendation: Add the length check to BOTH copies: `returndata.length == 0 || (returndata.length >= 32 && abi.decode(returndata, (bool)))`. Fixing the house helper in PhlimboV3 alone will NOT fix the migrator — the code is duplicated, not shared.
findings.distinctnessNote: CRITICAL: DISTINCT from V3-L-02 and V3-F-02 (both `src/PhlimboV3.sol:_tryTransfer/batchClaim`). This instance is `src/MigratorV2V3.sol:_tryTransfer/migrate` — different contract, different call site, different blast radius (migration pass vs flush chunk), newly introduced at ef98cd9. Do NOT collapse into V3-L-02/V3-F-02 as a duplicate; it is a replication of the class into a new contract by a fix commit.
crossRefs: V3-L-02 (open) — same root-cause class, PhlimboV3 instance, owns that contract's DoS severity
V3-F-02 (open) — the faithfulness twin of V3-L-02
V3-M-01 (fix-pending) — this is the residual brick path that survives story-025's fix
findings.sanitizerNote: Do NOT auto-suppress under the C4 known-invalid 'non-standard/weird ERC-20 tokens'. The prior run already adjudicated this exact class as in-scope Low (V3-L-02 open, V3-F-02 open) on the grounds that promoToken is an arbitrary owner-selected token the contract does not constrain beyond `!= phUSD && != rewardToken`. Additionally, the deviation here is doc-vs-code and holds regardless of token realism: the NatSpec's guarantee is unconditional.

findings.specText: CONFLICTING SPEC. (i) src/MigratorV2V3.sol:63-68 (header, rewritten by story-025): "`withdrawAll` remains a LAST-DITCH escape hatch: it sweeps this contract's ENTIRE phUSD, reward-token and (live) promo-token balances, INCLUDING amounts banked in `unclaimable`, leaving those claims unbacked. Reimbursing affected users after such a sweep is an out-of-band owner obligation." (ii) src/MigratorV2V3.sol:239 (function @dev, NOT updated by story-025): "Pure recovery sweep of stranded balances."
findings.specSource: git commit ef98cd9 body ("Rewrite the recovery-note NatSpec (audit F-01): ... document the banked-claims trade-off") + src/MigratorV2V3.sol header vs function @dev
findings.actualBehavior: story-025 rewrote the CONTRACT-LEVEL header and the INTERFACE NatSpec to disclose that withdrawAll confiscates banked user claims, but left withdrawAll's own function-level @dev (L239) reading "Pure recovery sweep of stranded balances" — describing the pre-story-025 behaviour, when the contract only ever held rewards transiently within a single tx and a sweep genuinely could not touch user-owed value. The two docs now contradict each other on the single most consequential property of the function, and the stale one sits directly above the code.
findings.deviation: The story's own bullet — 'document the banked-claims trade-off' — is only partially executed: the trade-off is documented in two of the three places that describe withdrawAll, and the one left stale is the one an owner reads at the call site. Compounding it, story-025 introduced a new class of contract-held liability (per-user banked `unclaimable`) with NO aggregate accounting: there is no `totalUnclaimable[token]`, no aggregate view, and no enumeration. The owner therefore cannot determine, before or after calling withdrawAll, WHETHER the sweep stranded anything or WHOM to reimburse — the 'out-of-band owner obligation' the NatSpec assigns them is not dischargeable from on-chain state alone (it requires off-chain RewardForwardFailed replay, netted against UnclaimableClaimed).
findings.law3FootgunAnalysis: Would a competent, NON-MALICIOUS owner be surprised? The DESIGN CHOICE itself (unconditional sweep) is deliberate, documented, and strictly more generous than the house baseline — PhlimboV3.finalizePromotion likewise sweeps unclaimablePromo to leftoverRecipient and zeroes it, forfeiting banked claims with no per-user claim at all. Law 3 trusts that choice and this finding does NOT contest it. The SURPRISE is the invisibility: PhlimboV3 exposes its banked liability as the aggregate view `unclaimablePromo()` and SolvencyDetermination.md §5 elevates it to a term any observer can check ('promoToken.balanceOf(phlimbo) − promoRewardBalance − Σ pendingPromo − unclaimablePromo >= 0'). The migrator copied the helper but not the liability-accounting discipline, and is absent from the solvency doc entirely. An owner sweeping dust after a completed pass — withdrawAll's original innocuous purpose, still asserted verbatim at L239 — has no on-chain signal that anything is owed, and the resulting failed claim surfaces to the user as a generic ERC20 insufficient-balance revert, not as 'swept'. Surprise ⇒ footgun ⇒ in scope as an operational hazard.
findings.impactNote: Low. Owner-action-gated, no unprivileged attacker path, no theft, bounded by banked amounts, reversible by owner reimbursement. NOT a Law-1 story-unsafe escalation.
findings.recommendation: (1) Update the L239 @dev to match the header — one line, removes a direct contradiction. (2) Add `mapping(address => uint256) public totalUnclaimable` maintained in _forward/claimUnclaimable, so the liability is visible before a sweep and the out-of-band reimbursement obligation is dischargeable on-chain. Optionally have withdrawAll sweep `balance - totalUnclaimable[token]`, which preserves the hatch while keeping claims backed — but that IS a design change and is the owner's call under Law 3.

findings.specText: story-024 (d61a7a3): "Freeze accPromoPerShare during Flushing at the accrual site". SolvencyDetermination.md §4: "`abortFlush` is solvency-neutral: `batchClaim` payments were correct early claims, so returning to Active leaves state consistent." src/PhlimboV3.sol:499-500: "Always safe: batchClaim is just early forced claims with debts correctly aligned, so a partial flush leaves fully consistent state."
findings.specSource: git commit d61a7a3 body + lib/phlimbo-ea/SolvencyDetermination.md §4 + src/PhlimboV3.sol abortFlush @dev
findings.actualBehavior: The gate skips promo accrual during Flushing but `_updatePool` still advances `lastRewardTime = block.timestamp` unconditionally (L768). Neither batchClaim, finalizePromotion, nor abortFlush calls `_updatePool` (verified). So on the abortFlush path, whether stakers are paid for the flush window depends on whether ANYONE happened to call `_updatePool` during it: if nobody did, `lastRewardTime` is still the beginFlush timestamp and the whole window accrues retroactively once the phase returns to Active; if someone did, that elapsed promo time is permanently skipped and its tokens remain in promoRewardBalance, ultimately reaching leftoverRecipient at the eventual finalize. `collectReward` is permissionless and gated only on `amount > 0`, so any third party can force the second outcome for ~1 wei of rewardToken immediately before an abortFlush.
findings.deviation: Not a contradiction of any explicit criterion — the story specifies the freeze, not the abort semantics, and solvency-neutrality DOES still hold (retro-accrual is capped by promoRewardBalance and fully balance-conserving; nothing is over-distributed). This is a behavioural side effect the gate INTRODUCED and the story did not consider: pre-gate, promo accrual across a flush window was continuous and path-independent (that was V3-H-01); post-gate, the flush window's promo accrual on the abort path is path-dependent on an unprivileged caller. The documented claim that abortFlush 'leaves fully consistent state' is true for solvency but silent on this distribution non-determinism.
findings.impactNote: Low, and I am deliberately not rating it higher. Grief-only with ZERO attacker profit (value moves from stakers to the owner-chosen leftoverRecipient, never to the caller). Bounded by promoRewardPerSecond × flush duration, and flush windows are short owner-driven operations. Affects the abort path ONLY — on the normal finalize path the window is skipped regardless, which is the intended freeze semantic. Surfaced per Law 1 (recall over tidiness) rather than suppressed; flagged for the econ/severity lane to weigh, and I would not object to QA.
findings.recommendation: Either call `_updatePool()` inside `abortFlush` before restoring phase Active (making the window deterministically skipped, matching the finalize path), or document that an aborted flush's promo window is intentionally path-dependent. The former is one line and removes the non-determinism entirely.

findings.specText: src/MigratorV2V3.sol:63-65 (story-025): "`withdrawAll` remains a LAST-DITCH escape hatch: it sweeps this contract's ENTIRE phUSD, reward-token and (live) promo-token balances". Commit ef98cd9: "Extend withdrawAll to sweep the live promo token".
findings.specSource: git commit ef98cd9 body + src/MigratorV2V3.sol header NatSpec
findings.actualBehavior: withdrawAll reads only the LIVE promo slot (`phlimboV3.promoToken()`, L250). A RETIRED promo token — one banked into `unclaimable[tokenA][user]` during promo A, after PhlimboV3.finalizePromotion has zeroed promoToken and promo B has started — is permanently unsweepable by the owner, and is claimable only by the affected user via claimUnclaimable. If that user is permanently blocked, the balance is stranded forever with no recovery path.
findings.deviation: Faithful to the letter (the story and NatSpec both say 'live', and the parenthetical is accurate), so this is NOT a story violation. It is a coverage gap in the 'LAST-DITCH escape hatch' narrative: the hatch cannot recover every token the contract can hold. Filed as informational for completeness.
findings.impactNote: QA/informational. Narrow reachability (requires a failed forward during promo A plus a rotation to promo B), dust-scale, and the gap is user-protective rather than harmful — it is the mirror image of F-08-02. Explicitly low-value; do not promote.

explicitlyNotFindings: story-024 gate composition with startPromotion — VERIFIED SAFE, not a finding. startPromotion calls _updatePool() BEFORE assigning promoToken (and finalize zeroes promoToken), so a stale lastRewardTime spanning a flush window cannot retro-accrue against the NEXT promo token. This was the most plausible way to reintroduce V3-H-01 and it is closed.
story-025 trade-off (b) (_forward banking) — VERIFIED SAFE, not a finding. See tradeOffAssessment.

withdrawAll's new external call to phlimboV3.promoToken() coupling the escape hatch to V3's liveness — considered and REJECTED as a finding. phlimboV3 is immutable and set to a real V3 at construction; promoToken() is a plain public getter that cannot realistically revert. Noted only so a future run does not re-derive it.

WithdrawnAll ABI widening (address,uint256,uint256) → (address,uint256,uint256,uint256) — declared in the story, so NOT scope creep. Flagged only as a cross-repo coordination note: any phoenix-phase-2-staging indexer decoding this event needs the new signature. No evidence of such a consumer was found in this repo; not filed as a finding to avoid speculation.

claimUnclaimable's arbitrary `token` parameter — considered and REJECTED. unclaimable[token][msg.sender] can only be non-zero for phUSD/rewardToken/promoToken, and amount==0 reverts, so an attacker-supplied token address is inert.
